transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Liam (CSM), Elena (Harborlane Head of Cloud), Samir (Platform), Priya (Security), Jonas (Product)

Summary: quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, VPC/KMS constraints, pilot perf plan, pricing SKU mapping and operational runbook. Focused on network egress, KMS integration pattern (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood-managed), and ops handoff for UAT/monitoring.

00:00 - Maya: okay thanks everyone for joining, i think we have a tight agenda — networking constraints, kms/key mgmt, uat/ops + listing metadata. we'll try to keep to about 45 minutes.
02:14 - Elena: thanks maya. just to set context, we run a multi-tenant platform for maritime logistics, low latency is important for some of our inference use cases but security/compliance is higher priority, so we prefer private deployments or marketplace listing that can be deployed into our cloud account.
03:02 - Maya: makes sense, we usually recommend Redwood Private via marketplace listing for that flow — you can deploy the control plane outside and connect to our runtime, or the packaged connector in your VPC.
03:45 - Diego: quick note, when folks say private, there are a couple of patterns we support: full Private (control plane in customer VPC), dedicated pools (Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering) or a marketplace-onramp package which installs a connector helm chart. each has tradeoffs for egress, kms, and observability.
04:33 - Samir: can you say more about the helm chart pattern? our security team wants to manage keys in our KMS, not Redwood's.
05:10 - Diego: yeah so the marketplace package includes an optional KMS integration layer — we support BYOK via customer KMS (AWS KMS or GCP CMEK). currently the helm values allow you to point at a key ARN and configure KMS grants, but there are a couple of nuances: token encryption at rest for model KV cache, and also audit logs.
06:05 - Priya: that was my question — audit logs and key rotation. do we require cross-account grants? any manual steps?
06:34 - Diego: good Q. for AWS the recommended pattern is cross-account grant with a service principal we document. there is a one-time grant step and we also recommend using a short-lived role for the connector to call KMS. rotation is customer-managed; Redwood doesn't rotate customer keys. we do support envelope encryption too.
07:20 - Priya: envelope encryption helps; we need to document key rotation policy for legal. can you send that?
07:33 - Maya: noted, will send KMS playbook.
08:05 - Jonas: on the marketplace listing metadata — what needs to be included so it passes the cloud vendor listing checklist? images, screenshots, network requirements?
08:27 - Liam: from ops standpoint we need the manifest: required ports, peering IP ranges, minimum instance types, and a test harness for marketplace verification. also billing SKU naming — that one trips people up.
09:05 - Maya: yes we have a packaging checklist for marketplace vendors, we'll attach a sample. for billing we can map to usage-based and reserved SKU, but Harborlane wants predictable costs — maybe a reserved capacity commit is the right option.
09:48 - Elena: reserved capacity could work but we need the pricing bands and expected SLAs. can Redwood commit to a latency SLO for the on-prem/connector pattern?
10:10 - Diego: latency SLO depends on deployment topology. if connector is in your VPC talking to our dedicated pools in the same region, we can SLO 99th percentile for <150ms for standard models; if you're fully on-prem and using private runtime, that's a separate engagement. we should capture the model family and token lengths — that impacts kernel selection and batching.
11:05 - Samir: our expected tail is often during batch ingest windows — we'll send qps and token-length histograms but rough numbers now: baseline 30 qps, spikes to 400 qps during reports, median token length 40, max 800 in rare batch jobs.
11:40 - Diego: got it — those long sequences change kernel selection and memory footprint. for marketplace packaging we'll include recommended quantization profile for the common model family to reduce memory during spike windows.
12:10 - Priya: two compliance items — data residency for EU customers, and export control for models with certain weights. Does the marketplace package let us choose region pinning?
12:35 - Diego: yes we support region pinning for Private and Dedicated. Hosted listings default to Redwood regions; the marketplace onramp deploys a chart into your region so residency is kept. we will note region-selection in the listing manifest.
13:00 - Jonas: what about observability — we need traces and token-level cost breakdowns visible in our console. is there a way to export traces to our telemetry stack?
13:25 - Liam: we have an OTLP exporter in the connector and can forward traces and metrics to your telemetry endpoint. we also support S3 or GCS log sinks for request/response payloads if you opt in. note: exporting request payloads may need additional legal approvals.
14:02 - Elena: okay good. Kingston (our legal) will ask about payload retention and re-identification risk.
14:20 - Maya: we'll include the data retention settings in the runbook and the checklist for legal review.
15:05 - Samir: networking specifics — what ports and NATs do we need? does the connector initiate outbound only?
15:40 - Diego: connector initiates outbound to Redwood endpoints by default — simple for firewall rules. For peering pattern there's also inbound rules for health checks. Required ports: 443/tcp egress, additional health-check over 9411 optional, and a control plane port if you choose dedicated peering. We'll list IP ranges in the manifest but we usually recommend egress-only to avoid complex NAT config.
16:25 - Priya: egress-only is preferred. any data egress costs we should plan for?
16:40 - Maya: egress costs depend on cloud and routing. if you deploy the runtime in your account the egress is internal. if you use Redwood Dedicated there may be cross-account transfer fees; we'll include estimates in the pricing doc.
17:10 - Jonas: we also need a short pilot plan — what does Redwood expect for the 3-day perf run?
17:45 - Diego: typical pilot: 3 days in staging, we run synthetic and real prompt sets, collect latency and token-cost metrics, verify KV cache hit rates, and evaluate failure cases. we'll need sample prompts, an auth token, and access to your staging telemetry. we'll provide a runbook and a benchmarking spreadsheet.
18:30 - Samir: good. about KV cache — will it be persisted to our disk? how do we handle snapshots?
18:55 - Diego: KV cache persists in memory and optional local disk snapshotting in the connector. for long seqs you can opt to checkpoint to a customer-managed blob store. snapshots are retained according to your retention settings; we can integrate with your lifecycle policies.
19:40 - Elena: any known gotchas with helm chart upgrades and UAT? we prefer rolling upgrades with minimal downtime.
20:05 - Diego: our chart supports canary / blue-green via Helm hooks; however stateful components (like cache) need careful coordination. we generally advise draining traffic and validating checkpoint restore in a non-prod cluster first. we'll add upgrade notes to the ops runbook.
21:00 - Priya: security review — does Redwood require admin-level IAM roles to install the connector? we want least privilege templates.
21:20 - Diego: we provide least-privilege iam templates (CloudFormation/Terraform) with narrow policies. installation requires a service role with KMS decrypt and permission to create ENIs for peering, but we can scope to resource ARNs. We'll share IAM policy samples.
22:05 - Maya: action item: Diego will attach IAM templates and helm values references.
22:26 - Jonas: what about marketplace listing visibility — metadata, screenshots and support contacts?
22:43 - Liam: include documentation link, contact info for integration support, a short FAQ, and a troubleshooting section. also include a brief performance benchmark matrix per instance type.
23:20 - Elena: procurement question — we have to evaluate CloudEndpoint and ZephyrAI too. bluntly, cost and ease of deployment will swing decision. what is the typical ramp timeline for teams like ours?
23:50 - Maya: for companies with an engineering owner and staging environment, a pilot to production can be 4-8 weeks depending on compliance checks. reserved capacity procurement adds another 2-4 weeks for contract and billing.
24:30 - Samir: about routing policy — can requests be routed to cheaper model variants automatically if capacity hits a limit?
24:55 - Diego: yes, Redwood supports smart routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. that requires mapping in the routing config and a compatibility matrix which we'll provide.
25:30 - Priya: do you do any on-the-fly quantization or is that a pre-deploy artifact?
25:50 - Diego: quantization profiles are applied during model onboarding and packaging; runtime supports a few dynamic paths but heavy quantization is part of the artifact. we'll recommend profiles based on your workload.
26:30 - Jonas: one more: test harness for marketplace verification — do you have an automated acceptance script we can run in CI?
26:55 - Liam: yes we publish an acceptance test suite (bash/python) you can run: checks for ports, IAM, smoke requests and a perf sanity run — we can point to the repo.
27:20 - Elena: great. can we get a mock listing page copy to review?
27:40 - Maya: yes i'll draft a listing blurb and screenshots.
28:05 - interruption (muffled): random network glitch, reconnecting...
29:12 - Diego: back — small audio hiccup.
29:40 - Priya: legal will also want an SLA template and an incident response contact list. can you provide those?
30:05 - Maya: yes, we'll provide an SLA template and an incident response playbook.
30:45 - Samir: for the pilot, we need debug-level logs for a day to troubleshoot caching behavior — is that feasible?
31:10 - Diego: feasible, but note debug logs include PII if request payloads are logged. we'll work with Priya to agree redaction rules and retention.
31:50 - Priya: agreed, we'll define redaction rules.
32:20 - Jonas: who is our single point of contact at Redwood once we start the pilot?
32:35 - Maya: i'll be primary AE, diego is SE for technical onboarding, and liam will handle post-provision ops handover.
33:00 - Maya: recap next steps: maya send listing draft, diego send IAM/KMS runbook and benchmarking spreadsheet, priya confirm KMS requirements, samir share traffic histograms, schedule pilot for week of 2026-05-25.
33:30 - Elena: sounds good. any blockers on Redwood side?
33:45 - Diego: only that we need the staging credentials and access to a sample dataset; otherwise workstreams are clear.
34:05 - Samir: we'll provision a staging namespace and send creds by 2026-05-17.
34:25 - Priya: i'll coordinate legal review and aim to get comments by 2026-05-21.
34:50 - Maya: noted.
35:20 - quick informal discussion about pricing bands and example reserved commit sizes
36:10 - Maya: example commit: 6-month reserved pool for predictable load we can map to an X GPU tier; pricing doc will show per-token and per-hour equivalents.
36:45 - Jonas: okay let's see the spreadsheet.
37:10 - Liam: logistcs note: for the marketplace cert we need a UAT run with the vendor partner team — that usually takes a day of validation.
37:45 - Diego: and an automated acceptance test run. we'll coordinate that.
38:10 - Elena: thanks all, this was helpful. one ask: can you include an estimate of total monthly cost under the three patterns: hosted, dedicated-peering, and private in your pricing email?
38:40 - Maya: yes i will include ballpark monthly numbers for typical instance sizes and bandwidth assumptions.
39:05 - Samir: also include estimated time to onboard a model family (open Llama variant) with quantization recommended.
39:25 - Diego: will do — we'll propose a quant/compile timeline.
40:00 - short wrap up and confirm mailing list for docs
40:20 - Maya: i'll send a follow-up to harborlane-infra@harborlane.com with attachments and scheduling link for the pilot.
40:40 - Elena: great. thanks everyone.
41:00 - meeting ends with informal chat about coffee and summer internships (off-topic)

Notes: Several minor transcription errors present (names occasionally misattributed). References to product names like KV cache, marketplace onramp, connector, dedicated pools and Redwood Private may be slightly mangled in places — please refer to attached runbook that Diego will share.
